summary: The bill amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to prohibit labeling any food with egg or egg product names unless it consists solely of the reproductive output of avian poultry (or meets existing egg product standards in regulation), and requires FDA to issue enforcement guidance within one year plus report to Congress on warnings and penalties issued.

scores.thoughts: The bill directs the FDA to issue guidance and enforce labeling rules for egg products, including reporting requirements. This entails minor administrative and enforcement activity but does not authorize new appropriations, expand or contract any program budgets, or alter overall federal spending levels.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue collection.

While the findings reference nutrition and Dietary Guidelines, the operative text is limited to food labeling definitions and enforcement. It does not address insurance coverage, provider reimbursement, public vs. private delivery systems, or any other healthcare policy dimension.
No provisions address firearms, ammunition, or related regulations.
No provisions address visas, border security, asylum, or immigration enforcement.
No provisions address reproductive health services or abortion access.
No provisions address defense budgets, military procurement, or national security spending.
The bill regulates labeling of egg alternatives but does not create, modify, or repeal any environmental standards, emissions rules, or conservation measures.
No provisions affect eligibility, funding, or administration of SNAP, TANF, Medicaid, or other welfare programs.
No provisions address schools, curricula, student aid, or education funding.
No provisions address controlled substances, decriminalization, or drug enforcement.

The bill references existing civil and criminal penalties under the FD&C Act for misbranding, but this is incidental enforcement language rather than any reform or expansion of sentencing or policing policy.
The bill applies to interstate commerce but does not alter tariffs, trade agreements, import quotas, or trade enforcement mechanisms.
No provisions address deficits, debt ceilings, or fiscal targets.
No provisions address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions address foreign assistance programs or funding.
No provisions address voting access, election administration, or campaign finance.
No provisions address data privacy, technology regulation, or surveillance.
No provisions address collective bargaining, worker protections, or union rights.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
